prompt: A teammate reads the change line by line and asks why a null check was removed.
tells: reads the change line by line
why: A teammate reading the change line by line and asking why something changed is code review. It catches risky edits like a removed safety check before they merge.
trap: The PR is where; reading and questioning is review.

prompt: A reviewer suggests a clearer variable name and approves.
why: Another developer looks over the change, suggests an improvement and approves it. That's code review, which covers readability as well as bugs.

prompt: Before merging, a second person must look over the change.
tells: a second person must look over the change
why: A required second pair of eyes before merging is code review. Many teams block merges until someone has approved.
trap: CI is automated; this is a person.

prompt: A senior leaves comments that teach a junior a safer way to write the loop.
why: Review comments aren't only for catching bugs; they spread better habits across the team. A senior teaching through comments is code review.
trap: The junior isn't asking; the senior is reviewing.

prompt: The reviewer spots a missing test for the empty-list case.
why: The reviewer noticed a case the author didn't cover. Spotting gaps like missing tests is a big part of code review.
trap: The test doesn't exist yet; the reviewer found the gap.

prompt: Keeping changes small makes them faster for teammates to check.
why: Small changes are quicker to read and easier to get right. Keeping them small is about making code review work well.
trap: Teammates checking is review, not CI.
